problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Minimize F(m,C)=E[V(m+Cξ)]−∑ᵢlog Cᵢᵢ, with ξ∼N(0,I_d), over locations m and lower-triangular factors C with positive diagonal and prescribed zero entries. The feasible parameter set and objective are convex.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/GaussianVariationalInference.lean: noiseLaw, sample, objective, IsCholesky; LongTails/Setups/StructuredGaussianVariationalInference.lean: InFamily, spec.admissible.

problem_class.label: strongly_convex
problem_class.details: The potential V has an L-Lipschitz gradient and μ-strongly monotone gradient, where 0<μ≤L. Gaussian averaging transfers μ-strong convexity to the location and scale parameters in the Euclidean/Frobenius metric.

problem_class.label: composite
problem_class.details: The objective combines the smooth expected potential E[V(m+Cξ)] with the convex negative-log-diagonal term and the prescribed sparsity constraints.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: Each query x∈ℝᵈ returns exactly ∇V(x), independently of history and oracle seed. The oracle supplies neither function values nor Gaussian expectations nor Hessians. All Params fields are public; V is the hidden instance. The extracted budget counts pointwise gradient calls.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StructuredGaussianVariationalInference.lean: spec.Query, spec.Reply, spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.Instance, spec.admissible; LongTails/Template.lean: executeWithTrace, Convergence.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The potential is defined on Euclidean ℝᵈ. Variational parameters comprise a location vector and a d×d scale matrix, with squared distance equal to the sum of squared location and Frobenius distances.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: A public pattern S satisfies i∈S(i), j≤i for j∈S(i), and |S(i)|≤w. Feasible covariance factors have positive diagonal and Cᵢⱼ=0 whenever j∉S(i). A family minimizer exists within squared parameter distance R² of the public feasible initialization (m0,C0), with R≥0. No additional assumptions are imposed on the sparsity of V.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: For every family minimizer (m*,C*), the output objective gap is integrable and E[F(m_out,C_out)−F(m*,C*)]≤ε, where ε>0. The output must be measurable and its scale factor must belong to the prescribed family for every seed.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The objective-gap guarantee is in expectation over the product of the algorithm and oracle seed laws. Exact oracle replies do not require a deterministic algorithm.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: Gaussian variational inference with a prescribed sparse Cholesky covariance factor is an established constrained variational optimization formulation; this setup uses smooth strongly convex potentials, pointwise gradient access, and expected objective accuracy.
